normal.label: Normal Skin
normal.description: Balanced, well-hydrated skin with minimal issues. Small pores, smooth texture, and a healthy glow. Lucky you!
normal.am_notes: Focus on antioxidant protection and SPF. Light moisturizer works well.
normal.pm_notes: Great candidate for retinol or light exfoliation to maintain texture. Ceramides for overnight barrier support.

oily.label: Oily Skin
oily.description: Excess sebum production, especially through the T-zone. Prone to shine, enlarged pores, and breakouts.
oily.am_notes: Lightweight, gel-based moisturizer. Niacinamide or BHA to control oil. Always SPF — oil doesn't protect from UV.
oily.pm_notes: BHA or retinol to clear pores. Skip heavy creams — opt for lightweight hydrating serums.

dry.label: Dry Skin
dry.description: Lacks sufficient moisture and natural oils. Feels tight, may flake, and is prone to irritation and fine lines.
traits: Rare breakouts but prone to sensitivity
dry.am_notes: Prioritize rich hydration — hyaluronic acid, ceramides, and a thicker moisturizer. SPF is non-negotiable.
dry.pm_notes: Overnight hydrating masks or richer creams. If using retinol, sandwich it with moisturizer. Oils like squalane on top.

combination.label: Combination Skin
combination.description: An oily T-zone (forehead, nose, chin) with normal to dry cheeks. The most common skin type — requires zone-specific care.
combination.am_notes: Balancing is key — niacinamide works well for both zones. Lightweight hydration that won't over-grease the T-zone.
combination.pm_notes: BHA to address T-zone congestion. Richer moisturizer on cheeks if needed. Retinol works well for most combination skin.

sensitive.label: Sensitive Skin
sensitive.description: Reactive skin that flushes, stings, or breaks out in response to products, weather, or stress. Barrier function is often compromised.
traits: Stinging or burning with many products
Reacts to fragrance, alcohol, harsh actives
sensitive.am_notes: Minimal actives. Barrier-first approach — ceramides and centella. Mineral SPF to avoid chemical filter irritation.
sensitive.pm_notes: Focus on repair: ceramides, centella, squalane. Avoid retinol until barrier is strong. Patch-test everything.

acne_prone.label: Acne-Prone Skin
acne_prone.description: Regularly experiences breakouts — whiteheads, blackheads, or cystic acne. Often oily but can also be dry-acne. Needs targeted, non-comedogenic care.
traits: Can be oily OR dry — acne isn't only oily skin
Inflamed, red spots alongside non-inflamed ones
acne_prone.am_notes: Niacinamide + SPF combo is your best friend. Keep routine simple during active breakouts — don't pile on actives.
acne_prone.pm_notes: BHA to clear pores, benzoyl peroxide for active spots (spot-treat only). Introduce retinol slowly once inflammation is down.
